chapter_theme: Last songs at Thiruthanigai (திருத்தணிகை, 5 of 5): two confessions of infatuation with women, one asking for Murugan's feet before knowledge and life are lost, the other for the art of singing his praise instead of falling into womb after womb; the praise dwells on the town of Thanigai, whose towers clear the deeds of those who worship from afar and where those who chant Thiruppugazh gather.

300.reading: The poet describes the women on the street with bound breasts, long dark hair, speech like a young cuckoo, carp eyes and swinging earrings, seducers skilled in enchantment, and asks that, before he, lacking true knowledge and learning, fades in infatuation, loses his understanding and dies, Murugan grant him the feet, bright as a crore of suns, that the wise praise, coming on the peacock with the rooster banner. The praise names the vel that cut down Sura's warriors for the ghosts to drink their blood, and Thanigai with its areca, plantain and paddy, its groves on the slopes, its towers and halls whose golden dust scatters the deeds of those who worship from afar, and its festooned streets circled by the chariot.
300.nuance: தூரத் தொழுவார் வினை சிந்திடு ... கோபுர மண்டபம்: the shrine's towers remove the deeds even of those who bow from a distance, a claim for the place itself. மோகன விஞ்சையர்: the women are 'enchanters', practisers of a spell.

301.reading: The poet speaks of women whose breasts are kin to evil deeds and whose eyes rival Kama's arrows, and asks that, after going among them and sinking in sorrow, he not fall face down into every womb-pit where heavy care and birth sink, but be given the art of chanting the praise of the feet that learned poets set to music. The praise names Murugan who went to the millet field and embraced Valli of the bow-bearing hunters, whose vel split the mountain, dried the sea and opened Sura's chest, at Thanigai where those who are minded to chant Thiruppugazh gather.
301.nuance: கருக்குழி தோறும் கவிழாதே: each birth is a fall headlong into a womb-pit. திருப்புகழ் ஓதும் கருத்தினர் சேரும் திருத்தணி: the song names the book's own title as the chant of Thanigai's devotees. The battle line has an unflagged garble (புநக்முள).

links.note: Both close by naming the poet's own work at Thanigai: 299 has Murugan delight in the Tamil garland of Arunagirinathan, and 301 has Thanigai as the place where those who chant Thiruppugazh gather.

source_issues: Song 301: unflagged garble புநக்முள (line 12), perhaps புகைமூள ('smoke rising'); the same க்மு appears in song 299 (மிக்முள) where மூ is likely meant.
